questions.text: Which part of an animal cell contains the genetic material and controls the cell's activities?

feedback: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell

questions.solution: The nucleus contains the chromosomes (DNA) and controls the activities of the cell
questions.hint: Think about where the chromosomes are kept

questions.text: In which part of a cell do most of the reactions of aerobic respiration take place?

feedback: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, not respiration

questions.solution: Most of the reactions of aerobic respiration happen in the mitochondria, releasing energy
questions.hint: Which structure is often described as the site of energy release?

questions.text: Which cell structure is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.solution: Proteins are made (synthesised) on the ribosomes
questions.hint: These are tiny structures found in the cytoplasm and in all types of cell

questions.text: Name the green structures in plant cells where photosynthesis takes place. Give the name.

feedback.chlorophyll: Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside these structures — name the structure itself

questions.solution: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis
questions.hint: They are found mainly in leaf cells and are green because of the pigment inside them

questions.text: What is the name of the net movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration? Give the term.

feedback.osmosis: Osmosis is only about water moving across a partially permeable membrane
feedback.active transport: Active transport moves substances from a lower to a higher concentration, using energy

questions.solution: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration
questions.hint: This happens in gases and liquids and does not need energy from respiration

questions.text: What is the cell wall of a plant cell made of?

feedback: Chitin is found in fungal cell walls
Starch is a storage substance in plants

questions.solution: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, which strengthens the cell
questions.hint: It is a carbohydrate made by plants for strength, not for storage

questions.text: Which of these structures is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.solution: Plant cells have a cell wall (and often chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole); animal cells do not
questions.hint: Animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm, a cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes

questions.text: Which statement describes a prokaryotic cell such as a bacterium?

options: Its genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus
It has a nucleus surrounded by a membrane
It is always larger than an animal cell
feedback: That describes a eukaryotic cell such as a plant or animal cell

questions.solution: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus: their DNA is a single loop in the cytoplasm (often with plasmids)
questions.hint: Think about where the DNA is found in a bacterium

questions.text: Which type of cell division produces two genetically identical daughter cells?

feedback: Meiosis produces four genetically different gametes

questions.solution: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells, for growth and repair
questions.hint: This is the division used for growth and repair

questions.text: What is the name of the movement of water from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane? Give the term.

feedback.diffusion: Diffusion is the general term for particles spreading out — the term for water across a membrane is more specific

questions.solution: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane
questions.hint: It is a special case of diffusion that only involves water

questions.text: Which process uses energy from respiration to move substances against a concentration gradient?

feedback: Diffusion moves particles down a concentration gradient without using energy
Osmosis is the passive movement of water

questions.solution: Active transport moves substances from a lower to a higher concentration, using energy from respiration
questions.hint: Diffusion and osmosis are passive — they do not need energy

questions.text: What is the name for an undifferentiated cell that can divide to produce many types of specialised cell? Give the term.
questions.solution: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells that can become many different types of cell
questions.hint: They are found in embryos, in bone marrow and in plant meristems

questions.text: Which type of microscope can show ribosomes and the internal structure of mitochondria?
questions.solution: Electron microscopes have a much higher resolution, so they can show very small structures such as ribosomes
questions.hint: Think about which microscope has the higher resolution

questions.text: Cancer is the result of changes in cells that lead to uncontrolled cell division. Which type of cell division is uncontrolled? Give the term.

feedback.meiosis: Meiosis only makes gametes — body cells divide by the other type of cell division

questions.solution: In cancer, mitosis happens out of control and forms a tumour
questions.hint: It is the type of division body cells use for growth and repair

questions.text: A cell has a cell wall, a nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts. What type of cell is it?

feedback: Bacterial cells have no nucleus
Fungal cells have a cell wall but no chloroplasts

questions.solution: Chloroplasts and a cell wall, together with a nucleus, show it is a plant cell
questions.hint: Which type of cell has chloroplasts?

questions.text: A cell has a cell wall, a cell membrane and plasmids, but no nucleus. What type of cell is it?

feedback: Plant cells have a nucleus
Fungal cells such as yeast have a nucleus

questions.solution: No nucleus means it is a prokaryotic cell — a bacterial cell
questions.hint: Which type of cell has no nucleus?

questions.text: A potato cylinder is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What will happen to its mass?

feedback: Water moves towards the more concentrated solution, so it leaves the potato

questions.solution: The solution outside is more concentrated, so water leaves the potato cells by osmosis and the mass decreases
questions.hint: Which way will water move by osmosis — into or out of the potato?

questions.text: Root hair cells take in mineral ions from soil water, where the concentration of ions is lower than inside the cell. Name the process used. Give the term.

feedback.diffusion: Diffusion only moves particles from a higher to a lower concentration
feedback.osmosis: Osmosis is the movement of water, not mineral ions

questions.solution: Moving ions from a lower to a higher concentration needs energy, so it is active transport
questions.hint: The ions are moving against the concentration gradient

questions.text: Oxygen moves from the air in the alveoli into the blood. Which process is this?

feedback: Osmosis is only the movement of water

questions.solution: Oxygen diffuses from a high concentration in the alveoli to a lower concentration in the blood
questions.hint: Oxygen is a gas moving down its concentration gradient

questions.text: Which change would increase the rate of diffusion of a substance into a cell?
questions.solution: A bigger difference in concentration (steeper gradient) increases the rate of diffusion
questions.hint: Think about the factors that affect how fast particles spread out

questions.text: A plant cell is placed in pure water. Why does it not burst?

options: The cell wall resists the pressure of the water inside
The cell membrane stops all water entering
The vacuole pumps water out of the cell

questions.solution: Water enters by osmosis and the cell becomes turgid, but the strong cell wall stops it bursting
questions.hint: Which structure do plant cells have that animal cells do not?

questions.text: Name the tissue at the tips of plant roots and shoots that contains stem cells. Give the name of the tissue.
questions.solution: Meristem tissue at root and shoot tips contains stem cells that can become any type of plant cell
questions.hint: It is found where the plant is growing

questions.text: Cell X has a surface area of 24 µm² and a volume of 8 µm³. Cell Y has a surface area of 54 µm² and a volume of 27 µm³. Which statement is correct?

options: Cell X has the larger surface area to volume ratio
Cell Y has the larger surface area to volume ratio
Both cells have the same surface area to volume ratio
Cell Y has a surface area to volume ratio of 3 : 1

questions.solution: Cell X: 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so 3 : 1. Cell Y: 54 ÷ 27 = 2, so 2 : 1. Cell X has the larger ratio
questions.hint: Divide each surface area by its volume

questions.text: A bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes. Starting with one bacterium, how many bacteria will there be after 2 hours? Give the number.
questions.solution: 2 hours = 120 minutes = 6 divisions. 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64 bacteria
questions.hint: Work out how many times the bacteria divide in 2 hours first

questions.text: Potato cylinders were left in sugar solutions. The percentage change in mass was +8% in 0.0 mol/dm³, +2% in 0.2 mol/dm³, −4% in 0.4 mol/dm³ and −10% in 0.6 mol/dm³. Between which two concentrations would there be no change in mass?
questions.solution: The change goes from positive (+2%) to negative (−4%) between 0.2 and 0.4 mol/dm³, so zero change is between them
questions.hint: Find where the percentage change goes from positive to negative

questions.text: A muscle cell needs to release a lot of energy. Which cell structure would you expect it to contain in large numbers? Give the name.

feedback.ribosomes: Ribosomes make proteins — energy is released by respiration in a different structure

questions.solution: Muscle cells contain many mitochondria to carry out aerobic respiration and release energy
questions.hint: Which structure carries out the reactions of aerobic respiration?

questions.text: A student views a cell using a ×10 eyepiece lens and a ×40 objective lens. What is the total magnification?

feedback: Multiply the two magnifications — don't add them

questions.solution: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 40 = ×400
questions.hint: Multiply the magnifications of the two lenses

questions.text: Why can an electron microscope show more detail than a light microscope?

options: It can be used on living cells

questions.solution: Electron microscopes have a higher resolution, so they can show two very close points as separate
questions.hint: Detail depends on the ability to tell two points close together apart

questions.text: A plant cell loses so much water that its cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall. Give the term that describes this cell.

feedback.turgid: A turgid cell is swollen with water — this cell has lost water
feedback.flaccid: A flaccid cell is soft, but here the membrane has pulled away from the wall, which has a special name

questions.solution: A cell that has lost so much water that the membrane pulls away from the wall is plasmolysed
questions.hint: This happens when a plant cell is in a very concentrated solution

questions.text: Why do single-celled organisms not need specialised exchange surfaces or a transport system?

options: They have a large surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion across the membrane is fast enough
Their cell wall absorbs all the substances they need
They are too small to respire

questions.solution: A single cell has a large surface area compared with its volume, so diffusion meets its needs
questions.hint: Compare the surface area of a tiny organism with its volume

questions.text: Which statement about stem cells is correct?

options: Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into most types of human cell
Adult bone marrow stem cells can become any type of cell
Stem cells are only found in embryos
feedback: Adult stem cells can only form a limited range of cell types, such as blood cells
Meristem cells can differentiate into any type of plant cell

questions.solution: Embryonic stem cells can become most cell types; adult stem cells are more limited; meristems can form any plant cell
questions.hint: Compare stem cells from embryos, adults and plants

questions.text: A bag made of a membrane that lets water through but not sucrose contains a 10% sucrose solution. It is placed in pure water. After an hour the bag is heavier. Which explanation is correct?

options: Water moved into the bag by osmosis because the solution inside was more concentrated
Sucrose moved out of the bag by diffusion
Water moved out of the bag by active transport
Sucrose moved into the bag by osmosis

questions.solution: Only water can cross the membrane, so water moved by osmosis into the more concentrated solution inside the bag
questions.hint: Which molecules can cross the membrane?

questions.text: Why does active transport into root hair cells slow down if the soil has no oxygen?

options: The cells cannot respire aerobically to release the energy needed
Oxygen is the substance being transported
Water can no longer enter by osmosis
Mineral ions only dissolve when oxygen is present

questions.solution: Active transport needs energy from respiration; without oxygen, aerobic respiration cannot happen
questions.hint: What does active transport need that diffusion does not?

questions.text: What happens in a cell before it divides by mitosis?

options: The DNA is copied so that each chromosome forms two identical copies
The cell membrane breaks down permanently
feedback: Halving the chromosome number happens in meiosis, not mitosis

questions.solution: Before mitosis the cell grows, makes more sub-cellular structures and copies its DNA
questions.hint: Each new cell must receive a full set of chromosomes

questions.text: Fish gills have many thin filaments with a good blood supply. What do these features give the gills a large amount of? Give the term.
questions.solution: Many thin filaments give a large surface area, so gas exchange by diffusion is fast
questions.hint: Think about what makes diffusion across an exchange surface faster

questions.text: Cell P is a small cube and cell Q is a large cube of the same shape. Which cell has the larger surface area to volume ratio? Answer P or Q.

feedback.Q: The larger cube has more surface area in total, but much more volume — compare the ratio
feedback.cell Q: The larger cube has more surface area in total, but much more volume — compare the ratio

questions.solution: Smaller objects have a larger surface area compared with their volume, so cell P has the larger ratio
questions.hint: Try it with cubes of side 1 cm and 3 cm

questions.text: Which enzyme breaks down starch into sugars?

feedback: Protease breaks down proteins
Lipase breaks down lipids
Bile is not an enzyme

questions.solution: Amylase (a carbohydrase) breaks starch down into sugars
questions.hint: The name of the substrate is a clue: starch is a carbohydrate

questions.text: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?

feedback: Veins carry blood back to the heart

questions.solution: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure
questions.hint: Remember: A for Away

questions.text: Which organ produces bile? Give the name of the organ.

feedback.gall bladder: The gall bladder stores bile, but it is made in a different organ
feedback.gallbladder: The gall bladder stores bile, but it is made in a different organ

questions.solution: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder
questions.hint: It is a large organ in the abdomen that also stores glycogen

questions.text: What type of pathogen causes measles?
questions.solution: Measles is caused by a virus and is spread by droplets from coughs and sneezes
questions.hint: It cannot be treated with antibiotics

questions.text: What is the name of the process in which white blood cells engulf and digest pathogens? Give the term.
questions.solution: Some white blood cells (phagocytes) engulf and digest pathogens: this is phagocytosis
questions.hint: The cells that do this are called phagocytes

questions.text: Which part of the blood helps it to clot at a wound?
questions.solution: Platelets are fragments of cells that help the blood to clot
questions.hint: They are small fragments of cells, not whole cells

questions.text: Which gas do red blood cells carry from the lungs to the body tissues? Give the name.
questions.solution: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to the tissues
questions.hint: Haemoglobin binds to this gas in the lungs

questions.text: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood out to the whole body?

feedback: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs

questions.solution: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta and around the body
questions.hint: The ventricles pump blood out of the heart

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?

feedback: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart

questions.solution: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs
questions.hint: Arteries carry blood away from the heart

questions.text: Lipase breaks down lipids into glycerol and which other product? Give the name.
questions.solution: Lipase breaks lipids (fats and oils) down into fatty acids and glycerol
questions.hint: The other product is a type of acid

questions.text: What are antibiotics used to treat?
questions.solution: Antibiotics kill bacteria (or stop them growing); they do not work against viruses
questions.hint: Antibiotics do not affect viruses

questions.text: Name the plant tissue that carries water and mineral ions from the roots to the leaves. Give the name.

feedback.phloem: Phloem carries dissolved sugars — the other transport tissue carries water

questions.solution: Xylem tissue carries water and mineral ions up from the roots
questions.hint: It is made of hollow tubes of dead cells strengthened by lignin

questions.text: What is the job of the valves in veins?

options: To pump blood around the body
To exchange gases with the tissues

questions.solution: Blood in veins is at low pressure, so valves stop it flowing backwards
questions.hint: Blood in veins is at low pressure

questions.text: What is the name of the movement of dissolved sugars through the phloem? Give the term.

feedback.transpiration: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves, through the xylem
feedback.translation: Translation is a stage of making proteins at the ribosomes — the movement of sugars in the phloem has a different name

questions.solution: Translocation is the movement of dissolved sugars through the phloem
questions.hint: It is not the loss of water from leaves

questions.text: In the lungs, what are the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens called? Give the name.
questions.solution: Gas exchange happens in the alveoli, which give a large surface area
questions.hint: They are found at the ends of the bronchioles

questions.text: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid. What is one job of this acid?

options: It kills many pathogens in food
feedback: Starch is digested by amylase in the mouth and small intestine

questions.solution: Stomach acid kills many pathogens and gives the right pH for the protease enzyme there
questions.hint: It is part of the body's defence against disease

questions.text: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration?

feedback: Humid air reduces the concentration gradient, so transpiration slows down

questions.solution: Warmer conditions make water evaporate and diffuse out of leaves faster
questions.hint: Think about what makes water evaporate faster

questions.text: An enzyme is heated to 70 °C and stops working. What has happened to it?

options: Its active site has changed shape so the substrate no longer fits
It has turned into the substrate
feedback: Enzymes are proteins, not living things, so they cannot be killed — they are denatured

questions.solution: High temperature denatures the enzyme: the active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits
questions.hint: Enzymes are proteins with an active site

questions.text: Which disease is caused by a protist and spread by mosquitoes? Give the name.
questions.solution: Malaria is caused by a protist; mosquitoes are the vectors that spread it
questions.hint: It causes repeated bouts of fever

questions.text: A vaccine contains dead or inactive forms of a pathogen. What does it cause the body to produce?

feedback: Antibiotics are medicines — the body does not make them

questions.solution: White blood cells respond to the antigens by making antibodies and memory cells, giving immunity
questions.hint: Think about what white blood cells make in response to an antigen

questions.text: Which cells open and close the stomata on a leaf? Give the name of the cells.
questions.solution: A pair of guard cells surrounds each stoma and controls its opening and closing
questions.hint: They are found in pairs around each stoma

questions.text: Coronary heart disease is caused by a build-up of fatty material in which blood vessels?
questions.solution: Fatty material builds up in the coronary arteries, which supply the heart muscle with oxygen
questions.hint: These arteries supply the heart muscle itself

questions.text: An enzyme works fastest at pH 2. Where in the digestive system is it most likely to work?
questions.solution: pH 2 is strongly acidic, like the hydrochloric acid in the stomach
questions.hint: Which part of the digestive system is acidic?

questions.text: Starch and amylase are mixed. A drop of the mixture is tested with iodine every minute. It turns blue-black for the first 3 minutes, then stays orange-brown from 4 minutes onwards. What does this show?

options: All the starch had been broken down by 4 minutes

questions.solution: Iodine turns blue-black with starch; orange-brown from 4 minutes means no starch was left
questions.hint: What colour does iodine turn when starch is present?

questions.text: Use cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume. A person's heart rate is 72 beats per minute and their stroke volume is 70 cm³. Calculate the cardiac output in cm³ per minute. Give the number.
questions.solution: Cardiac output = 72 × 70 = 5040 cm³ per minute
questions.hint: Multiply the heart rate by the stroke volume

questions.text: The rate of water uptake of a plant was 4.2 cm³ per hour in still air and 7.8 cm³ per hour with a fan blowing. Which conclusion is supported?

options: Moving air increases the rate of transpiration
Moving air decreases the rate of transpiration
The fan increased the humidity around the leaves

questions.solution: The rate was higher with the fan, so moving air increases the rate of transpiration
questions.hint: Compare the two rates

questions.text: Why should antibiotics not be prescribed for a common cold?

options: Colds are caused by viruses, which antibiotics do not kill
Colds are caused by bacteria that are all resistant

questions.solution: Colds are viral; antibiotics only work on bacteria, and overuse helps resistant bacteria spread
questions.hint: What type of pathogen causes a cold?

questions.text: Amylase is made in the salivary glands and in one other organ, which also produces insulin. Name this organ.

feedback.liver: The liver makes bile, not amylase or insulin

questions.solution: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes, including amylase, and the hormone insulin
questions.hint: This organ is part of both the digestive system and the endocrine system

questions.text: The wall of the left ventricle is thicker than the wall of the right ventricle. Why?

options: It pumps blood all around the body, which needs a higher pressure
It receives blood from the lungs
It pumps blood only to the lungs
feedback: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs

questions.solution: The left ventricle pumps blood around the whole body, so it needs more muscle to produce a higher pressure
questions.hint: Compare where each ventricle pumps blood to

questions.text: Why are the walls of capillaries only one cell thick?

options: So substances can diffuse quickly between the blood and the tissues
So that blood flows at high pressure

questions.solution: Thin walls give a short diffusion distance, so substances are exchanged quickly
questions.hint: Capillaries are where substances are exchanged with the tissues

questions.text: Why should patients finish the full course of antibiotics they are prescribed?

options: To reduce the chance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria surviving and spreading
To kill any viruses as well
To make the body produce antibodies
To stop the antibiotic being stored in the liver

questions.solution: Finishing the course kills all the bacteria, so resistant strains are less likely to survive and spread
questions.hint: Think about which bacteria might survive if the course is stopped early

questions.text: When a large proportion of a population is vaccinated, unvaccinated people are less likely to catch the disease. What is this called?
questions.solution: Herd immunity: with most people immune, the pathogen is less likely to spread to anyone
questions.hint: It protects the whole group, not just the vaccinated people

questions.text: Why does an enzyme only catalyse one specific reaction?

options: Only one substrate has the right shape to fit its active site
It is made of only one amino acid
It is used up after one reaction
It only works at one temperature

questions.solution: The active site has a specific shape that only fits one substrate (lock and key)
questions.hint: Think about the shape of the active site

questions.text: In a double-blind drug trial, some patients receive a substance that contains no drug. What is this substance called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A placebo looks like the drug but contains no active drug; it lets scientists compare the real effect
questions.hint: It is used to compare with the real drug

questions.text: Why do root hair cells have a large surface area?

options: To increase the absorption of water and mineral ions
To transport sugars to the leaves
feedback: Root cells are underground and have no chloroplasts

questions.solution: A large surface area increases the rate of absorption of water (by osmosis) and mineral ions
questions.hint: What do root hair cells take in from the soil?

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the double circulatory system in humans?

options: Blood passes through the heart twice for each complete circuit of the body
Blood passes through the lungs twice in each circuit
The heart has only two chambers
Arteries and veins carry blood at the same pressure

questions.solution: One circuit goes heart → lungs → heart, the other heart → body → heart, so blood passes through the heart twice
questions.hint: Trace the path of the blood from the right ventricle

questions.text: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?

feedback: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis

questions.solution: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
questions.hint: Write the word equation for photosynthesis

questions.text: What are the products of aerobic respiration?

feedback: Those are the products of photosynthesis
That is anaerobic respiration in yeast

questions.solution: Aerobic respiration: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
questions.hint: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration

questions.text: What is the name of the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light? Give the name.

feedback.chloroplast: Chloroplasts are the structures — name the green pigment inside them
feedback.chloroplasts: Chloroplasts are the structures — name the green pigment inside them

questions.solution: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis
questions.hint: It is the substance that makes leaves green

questions.text: Which hormone lowers the blood glucose concentration?

feedback: Glucagon raises blood glucose

questions.solution: Insulin, from the pancreas, makes cells take up glucose, lowering blood glucose
questions.hint: It is released by the pancreas after a meal

questions.text: What is made in human muscles during anaerobic respiration? Give the name.

feedback.ethanol: Ethanol is made by anaerobic respiration in yeast and plants, not in human muscles

questions.solution: Anaerobic respiration in muscles: glucose → lactic acid
questions.hint: It builds up during hard exercise and causes muscle fatigue

questions.text: Which gland is often called the master gland?
questions.solution: The pituitary gland in the brain releases hormones that control other glands
questions.hint: It is in the brain and controls other glands

questions.text: What is the name for keeping the body's internal conditions constant? Give the term.
questions.solution: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose
questions.hint: The word comes from Greek for 'staying the same'

questions.text: Which type of respiration releases more energy from each glucose molecule?
questions.solution: Aerobic respiration releases much more energy because glucose is completely oxidised
questions.hint: Which type breaks glucose down completely?

questions.text: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast?

feedback: Lactic acid is made by anaerobic respiration in animal muscles

questions.solution: In yeast: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide (fermentation)
questions.hint: This process is used to make bread and beer

questions.text: Which part of the brain monitors and controls body temperature? Give the name.
questions.solution: The thermoregulatory centre in the hypothalamus monitors blood temperature
questions.hint: It contains receptors that are sensitive to the temperature of the blood

questions.text: Which neurone carries impulses from receptors to the central nervous system?

feedback: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors

questions.solution: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the central nervous system
questions.hint: Receptors detect stimuli

questions.text: Which hormone is released by the adrenal glands in times of fear or stress?
questions.solution: Adrenaline prepares the body for 'fight or flight'
questions.hint: It prepares the body for 'fight or flight'

questions.text: What is the name of the gap between two neurones? Give the term.
questions.solution: A synapse is the gap between neurones; chemicals diffuse across it to pass on the impulse
questions.hint: Chemicals diffuse across this gap

questions.text: What causes type 1 diabetes?

options: The pancreas does not produce enough insulin
Body cells no longer respond to insulin
The liver stores too much glycogen
feedback: That describes type 2 diabetes

questions.solution: In type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces too little insulin, so blood glucose can rise too high
questions.hint: Think about which organ makes insulin

questions.text: A plant is moved from a dim room into bright light. Carbon dioxide and temperature are not limiting. What happens to its rate of photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Light was the limiting factor, so more light increases the rate of photosynthesis
questions.hint: Which factor was limiting the rate in the dim room?

questions.text: During a sprint, a runner's muscles do not get enough oxygen. Which substance builds up in the muscles?
questions.solution: Without enough oxygen, muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up
questions.hint: Think about anaerobic respiration in animals

questions.text: You touch a hot pan and pull your hand away before you even feel the pain. What type of response is this? Give the term.
questions.solution: This is a reflex: a fast, automatic response that does not involve the conscious brain
questions.hint: It is fast and automatic

questions.text: In the reflex that pulls your hand away from a hot object, what is the effector?

feedback: The receptor detects the stimulus — the effector carries out the response

questions.solution: The effector is the muscle that contracts to move the hand away
questions.hint: The effector carries out the response

questions.text: Blood glucose concentration rises after a meal. What happens next?

options: The pancreas releases insulin and glucose moves into cells
The liver breaks down glycogen into glucose
feedback: Glucagon is released when blood glucose is too low

questions.solution: Insulin makes cells take up glucose and the liver store it as glycogen, so blood glucose falls
questions.hint: Which hormone lowers blood glucose?

questions.text: Plants convert the glucose made in photosynthesis into an insoluble substance for storage. Name this substance.
questions.solution: Glucose is stored as insoluble starch, which does not affect osmosis
questions.hint: Iodine solution turns blue-black when this substance is present

questions.text: Plants use glucose to make a substance that strengthens their cell walls. Name this substance.

feedback.starch: Starch is the storage substance — the cell wall substance is different
feedback.cellulase: Cellulase is an enzyme that breaks this substance down — name the substance itself

questions.solution: Glucose is used to make cellulose for cell walls
questions.hint: It is a long chain of glucose molecules that forms strong fibres

questions.text: As a lamp was moved closer to some pondweed, the rate of photosynthesis increased and then stayed the same. What is the most likely reason the rate stopped increasing?

options: Another factor, such as carbon dioxide concentration, had become limiting
Light intensity had become the limiting factor
The plant had run out of chlorophyll
The light had denatured all the enzymes

questions.solution: Once the rate stops rising with more light, something else (such as carbon dioxide or temperature) is limiting
questions.hint: If more light makes no difference, light is no longer the limiting factor

questions.text: After exercise, a person keeps breathing heavily for a few minutes. What is the extra oxygen used for?

options: To react with the lactic acid that built up (repaying the oxygen debt)
To make glucose in the lungs

questions.solution: The oxygen debt is the oxygen needed to deal with the lactic acid made during anaerobic respiration
questions.hint: Think about what built up in the muscles during exercise

questions.text: Which hormone does the pancreas release when the blood glucose concentration is too low? Give the name.

feedback.glycogen: Glycogen is the storage substance in the liver — name the hormone
feedback.insulin: Insulin lowers blood glucose — this hormone raises it

questions.solution: Glucagon makes the liver convert glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose
questions.hint: It has the opposite effect to insulin

questions.text: Which of these happens when a person is too hot?

options: Blood vessels near the skin surface constrict
Hairs on the skin stand up
feedback: Vasoconstriction keeps the body warm — it happens when you are cold

questions.solution: Sweat evaporates from the skin and transfers energy away, cooling the body
questions.hint: Which response transfers energy away from the skin?

questions.text: Pondweed gave 12 bubbles per minute at 20 °C, 24 at 30 °C, 30 at 40 °C and 4 at 50 °C. Which explanation fits the result at 50 °C?

options: Enzymes involved in photosynthesis were denatured
The light intensity was too low
There was too much carbon dioxide
The plant had too much chlorophyll

questions.solution: At 50 °C the enzymes that control photosynthesis are denatured, so the rate falls sharply
questions.hint: Photosynthesis is controlled by enzymes

questions.text: Which type of neurone connects sensory neurones to motor neurones in the spinal cord? Give the name.
questions.solution: Relay neurones in the spinal cord connect sensory neurones to motor neurones
questions.hint: It passes the impulse on inside the central nervous system

questions.text: Why do plants need nitrate ions from the soil?
questions.solution: Nitrate ions supply nitrogen, which plants combine with glucose to make amino acids and proteins
questions.hint: Starch and cellulose contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen

questions.text: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy than aerobic respiration?

options: Glucose is only partly broken down
feedback: Anaerobic respiration does not use oxygen at all

questions.solution: In anaerobic respiration glucose is not completely oxidised, so less energy is released
questions.hint: Compare the products: are they fully broken down?

questions.text: Which statement about type 2 diabetes is correct?

options: Body cells no longer respond properly to insulin
It is caused by a virus
It is always treated with insulin injections from birth
The pancreas stops making any insulin in childhood
feedback: That describes type 1 diabetes

questions.solution: In type 2 diabetes the body's cells stop responding properly to insulin
questions.hint: Compare the causes of type 1 and type 2 diabetes

questions.text: Why is a reflex action faster than a response that you think about?

options: The impulse does not have to pass through the conscious part of the brain

questions.solution: In a reflex arc the impulse passes through a relay neurone in the spinal cord, skipping the conscious brain
questions.hint: Trace the path of the impulse in a reflex arc

questions.text: The level of thyroxine in the blood is controlled by a process in which a change triggers a response that reverses the change. Give the term for this process.

feedback.positive feedback: Positive feedback would make the change bigger — this response reverses it

questions.solution: Negative feedback: if thyroxine rises, TSH release falls so less thyroxine is made, and the reverse
questions.hint: The response reverses the original change

questions.text: Muscles store glucose as glycogen. Why is this useful during exercise?

options: Glycogen can be converted back to glucose for respiration
Glycogen makes the muscle contract by itself

questions.solution: Stored glycogen is broken down to glucose, which the muscle cells use for respiration
questions.hint: What do muscle cells need glucose for?

questions.text: On a cold day, body temperature stays close to 37 °C. Which response helps to keep it there?

options: Muscles contract rapidly (shivering), releasing energy from respiration
Blood vessels near the skin dilate
feedback: Vasodilation transfers more energy to the surroundings — it happens when you are too hot

questions.solution: Shivering uses respiration to release energy, which warms the body
questions.hint: Which response would release energy inside the body?

questions.text: Why does the rate of photosynthesis of a plant in a field fall to almost zero at night?
questions.solution: Without light there is no energy for photosynthesis, so light intensity is the limiting factor
questions.hint: Which factor changes most between day and night?

questions.text: What is the structure of a DNA molecule?

options: Two strands twisted to form a double helix

questions.solution: DNA is a polymer made of two strands forming a double helix
questions.hint: Think of a twisted ladder

questions.text: What is the name for different versions of the same gene? Give the term.
questions.solution: Alleles are different forms of the same gene, for example for blue or brown eyes
questions.hint: One version is often dominant and the other recessive

questions.text: How many chromosomes are there in a normal human body cell?

feedback: 23 is the number in a gamete (egg or sperm)

questions.solution: Human body cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes, which is 46 chromosomes
questions.hint: Body cells have 23 pairs

questions.text: What is at the start of most food chains?

options: A producer, such as a green plant

questions.solution: Food chains start with a producer, which makes glucose by photosynthesis
questions.hint: Which organisms make their own food?

questions.text: Which scientist proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species'? Give the surname.

feedback.Mendel: Mendel studied inheritance in pea plants
feedback.Lamarck: Lamarck suggested a different idea: inheritance of acquired characteristics

questions.solution: Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859
questions.hint: He studied finches and other animals on the Galapagos Islands

questions.text: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere in the carbon cycle?

feedback: Respiration releases carbon dioxide
Combustion releases carbon dioxide

questions.solution: Plants and algae take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis
questions.hint: Which process in plants uses carbon dioxide?

questions.text: What is the name for all the populations of different species living in one habitat? Give the term.

feedback.population: A population is all the organisms of one species — this includes many species
feedback.ecosystem: An ecosystem also includes the non-living (abiotic) parts of the environment

questions.solution: A community is all the populations of different species in a habitat
questions.hint: A population is just one species

questions.text: What does the word 'genotype' mean?

options: The number of chromosomes in a cell
The species an organism belongs to
feedback: That is the phenotype

questions.solution: Genotype is the combination of alleles, for example Bb
questions.hint: Compare genotype and phenotype

questions.text: What term describes an organism that has two identical alleles for a gene, such as BB or bb? Give the term.

feedback.heterozygous: Heterozygous means two different alleles, such as Bb
feedback.homologous: Homologous describes a matching pair of chromosomes — two identical alleles has a different term

questions.solution: Homozygous means two identical alleles
questions.hint: 'Homo' means 'same'

questions.text: Which type of reproduction produces genetically identical offspring?
questions.solution: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and mitosis, so the offspring are clones
questions.hint: It involves only one parent

questions.text: What type of cell division produces gametes? Give the term.

feedback.mitosis: Mitosis makes identical body cells — gametes are made by a different division

questions.solution: Meiosis makes four genetically different gametes with half the number of chromosomes
questions.hint: This division halves the number of chromosomes

questions.text: In the name Homo sapiens, what does 'Homo' tell you?
questions.solution: In the binomial system, the first name is the genus and the second is the species
questions.hint: The binomial name has two parts

questions.text: Which of these is an abiotic factor?
questions.solution: Abiotic factors are non-living, such as temperature, light and water
questions.hint: 'Abiotic' means non-living

questions.text: What is a species?

options: A group of organisms that can breed together to produce fertile offspring
All the organisms living in one habitat
Organisms in the same food chain

questions.solution: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring
questions.hint: Think about breeding and fertile offspring

questions.text: What term describes a species that has no living members left? Give the term.

feedback.endangered: Endangered species are at risk, but some are still alive

questions.solution: A species is extinct when there are no individuals left alive
questions.hint: The dodo is an example

questions.text: Owls catch more white mice than brown mice on dark soil. Over many generations, what is most likely to happen?

options: Brown fur becomes more common in the population
Each mouse changes its fur colour during its life
feedback: Individuals don't change — the population changes over generations

questions.solution: Brown mice survive and breed more, passing on their alleles, so brown fur becomes more common
questions.hint: Which mice are more likely to survive and reproduce?

questions.text: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what is the rabbit?
questions.solution: The rabbit eats the producer (grass), so it is the primary consumer
questions.hint: Count the feeding levels from the start of the chain

questions.text: Two plants of the same species have different heights because one grew in the shade. What type of variation is this? Give the type.

feedback.genetic: The plants are the same species and the difference comes from the conditions, not the genes
feedback.genetic variation: The difference comes from the conditions they grew in, not their genes

questions.solution: The difference is caused by the conditions (light), so it is environmental variation
questions.hint: Is the cause the genes or the surroundings?

questions.text: Which organism did Gregor Mendel use in his experiments on inheritance?
questions.solution: Mendel bred pea plants and worked out the basic rules of inheritance
questions.hint: He was a monk with a garden

questions.text: Which human activity reduces biodiversity?
questions.solution: Deforestation destroys habitats, so many species are lost
questions.hint: Which activity destroys habitats?

questions.text: A bacterium survives an antibiotic because of a random change in its DNA. What is a random change in DNA called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A mutation is a random change in DNA; occasionally it gives resistance
questions.hint: These changes happen randomly and can create new alleles

questions.text: What is the term for humans breeding plants or animals for particular characteristics? Give the term.

feedback.natural selection: In natural selection the environment 'chooses' — here humans choose

questions.solution: Selective breeding (artificial selection) chooses parents with the desired characteristics
questions.hint: Humans choose which individuals breed

questions.text: A student counted daisies in five 1 m² quadrats: 3, 5, 4, 6 and 2. The field has an area of 200 m². What is the estimated number of daisies in the field?

feedback: 20 is the total in the quadrats — find the mean per m² and multiply by the area
Use the mean per quadrat (4), not the total (20)

questions.hint: Find the mean number per quadrat first

questions.text: Why is there less biomass at each higher trophic level in a food chain?

options: Some biomass is lost in waste and some is used in respiration
Animals at higher levels eat less often
Plants do not absorb all the sunlight

questions.solution: Biomass is lost as egested and excreted waste, and glucose is used in respiration, so less passes on
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the food an animal eats

questions.text: Producers in a food chain store 10 000 kJ of energy and the primary consumers get 1000 kJ. What percentage of the energy is passed on? Give the number.
questions.hint: Divide the energy passed on by the energy at the start, then multiply by 100

questions.text: How does antibiotic resistance spread in a population of bacteria?

options: A mutation gives resistance, resistant bacteria survive the antibiotic, then they reproduce
The antibiotic causes the mutation, then all bacteria survive
Bacteria learn to resist and teach other bacteria
Resistant bacteria die and the others reproduce

questions.solution: A random mutation gives resistance; resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, so resistance spreads
questions.hint: Mutations are random — the antibiotic does not cause them

questions.text: In a population of 500 snails, 350 have a dark shell. What percentage of the snails have a dark shell? Give the number.
questions.hint: Divide the number with a dark shell by the total, then multiply by 100

questions.text: Which statement about the carbon cycle is correct?

options: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
Respiration removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Decomposers take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis

questions.solution: Combustion of fossil fuels releases carbon that was stored for millions of years as carbon dioxide
questions.hint: Which processes release carbon dioxide and which remove it?

questions.text: In a predator–prey cycle, why does the number of predators rise soon after the number of prey rises?

options: There is more food, so more predators survive and reproduce
Predators eat less when prey is common

questions.solution: More prey means more food for predators, so more predators survive and breed — after a short delay
questions.hint: Think about food supply for the predators

questions.text: Why does sexual reproduction help a species to survive when the environment changes?

options: It produces variation, so some individuals may be suited to the new conditions
feedback: Identical offspring come from asexual reproduction

questions.solution: Variation means some individuals may survive the new conditions and pass on their alleles
questions.hint: Think about variation in the offspring

questions.text: Why was Darwin's theory of natural selection only gradually accepted?

options: There was little evidence at the time, and the mechanism of inheritance was not known
Darwin had no evidence at all
Natural selection was disproved in the 1900s
Scientists already knew all about genes and DNA

questions.solution: There was not enough evidence and genes were unknown; the theory also challenged the belief that God made all living things
questions.hint: Think about what scientists did not know in the 1800s

questions.text: In the three-domain system, living things are divided into Archaea, Bacteria and which other domain?
questions.solution: Carl Woese's three domains are Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota
questions.hint: This domain includes all organisms whose cells have a nucleus

questions.text: Why does decay happen fastest in warm, moist conditions with plenty of oxygen?

options: Decomposers grow and respire fastest in these conditions
Dead material is softer when warm
Oxygen breaks down the dead material by itself

questions.solution: Microorganisms need warmth, water and oxygen to grow, respire and digest dead material quickly
questions.hint: Decay is carried out by microorganisms

questions.text: Someone says that giraffes got long necks by stretching to reach leaves and then passing this on to their young. Whose idea is this?

feedback: Darwin's idea was natural selection of variation that already exists

questions.solution: Lamarck suggested that characteristics acquired during life are inherited — this is now known to be wrong
questions.hint: This idea is called the inheritance of acquired characteristics

questions.text: In genetic engineering, a small ring of DNA is used to carry a new gene into a bacterium. What is this ring called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Plasmids are small rings of DNA in bacteria; they are used as vectors in genetic engineering
questions.hint: Bacteria have these as well as their main loop of DNA

questions.text: A gene is a short section of DNA that codes for a particular sequence of amino acids. What does this sequence of amino acids make? Give the word.
questions.solution: The sequence of bases in a gene codes for the order of amino acids in a specific protein
questions.hint: Amino acids join together to make these molecules
